title: CLI --help text
when: A command line tool needs a clear --help output and usage error messages.
prompt:
Goal: A compact help screen that shows usage, every option with defaults and a few examples, printed by -h and --help.
Steps:
1. Line one: tool name and a one line description; line two: Usage: tool [options] <input> [output].
2. Options block aligned in columns: short and long form, value placeholder, description and (default: x).
3. Commands block when the tool has subcommands, each with one line, and tool help <command> for details.
4. Examples block with 2 or 3 real invocations and a short comment each.
5. Print help to stdout and exit 0 for --help; on bad usage print a one line error plus "Run tool --help" to stderr and exit 2.
6. Keep it under about 25 lines and 80 columns; add --version printing the version.
Quality bar:
- Help matches the parser exactly.
- Defaults are shown.
- Errors name the bad flag or value.
Pitfalls:
- Dumping help on every error.
- Help text that lists removed flags.
- Exit code 0 for bad usage.
Verify:
- [ ] --help prints usage and exits 0.
- [ ] Bad flags exit non zero with a short message.
- [ ] The script has a shebang.
- [ ] Scripts parse.
Output: The help string and usage error handling in the CLI source.

examples.output: Usage: imgsize [options] <dir>; -w, --width <px> (default: 1200); 3 examples; exit 2 on bad flags
